published_statement: GKLM p.12: 'Assuming that light travels on the brane with speed c while a bulk field propagates with speed c+Delta c, the velocity bound (6) directly translates to Delta c/c = gamma - 1 (38)'. Bound (6), p.2: 'bulk causality: |x'| <= gamma t' ... The bulk bound is generically saturated at late times (large t')'. Data quoted with it: GW170817/GRB 170817A [17] '-3 x 10^-15 <= Delta c/c <= +7 x 10^-16 (39)'. The hedge, verbatim: 'If we entertain the possibility that these are bulk degrees of freedom, the bounds on brane velocity become very strict.' ('these' = the SN1987A antineutrinos and the gravitational waves of the preceding sentences.) GKLM print no numerical beta bound.
published_hypotheses: H1 flat bulk: d-dimensional Minkowski with ONE spatial dimension compactified on a circle, z ~ z + 2 pi R (eq. 1, M4 x S1); no bulk curvature, no warping

H2 the brane is a test hyperplane at z' = 0 moving at constant beta purely along the compact direction (z = beta t in the preferred frame; eq. 2-4); untilted (spans all non-compact directions); induced metric exactly Minkowski

H3 the observer is at rest in the brane frame (t', x') -- i.e. no velocity along the brane relative to the preferred frame (GKLP's B = 0; GKLP 2208.09014 eq. 20: 'For B = 0, this reduces to the result v = gamma found in [1]')
H4 light is brane-confined and travels at c on the brane ('Assuming that light travels on the brane with speed c')
H5 the messenger is a bulk field propagating causally in the bulk (free, linear; Green's-function analysis)
H6 late times / high momentum: bound (6) is 'generically saturated at late times'; KK modes approach v_g -> gamma only as |k'| -> infinity (eq. 37)
H7 whether neutrinos or gravitons ARE bulk degrees of freedom is entertained, not asserted ('If we entertain the possibility')
H8 brane-localized matter 'would presumably respect' worldvolume Lorentz symmetry (p.3) -- a presumption, not a theorem

GKLM p.3 say brane-localized matter 'would presumably respect' the would-be Lorentz symmetry; Kabat & Nomura arXiv:2309.05759 (abstract, READ via cached alphaXiv text) show bulk loops with non-zero winding generate UV-finite Lorentz-violating terms in the brane effective action -- and branelink.py:96-97 itself computes such a loop-induced SME coefficient (|c| <= 6.37e-64). So 'identically' holds at tree level only; the magnitude is immaterial to the dichotomy (a DISCREPANCY of wording, not a refutation).

lacked_data: What GKLM had (Jul 2022): the GW170817/GRB 170817A bound as published in 2017 (26 Mpc, 0-10 s window), the SN1987A neutrino bounds, and no measurement of any observer velocity B along the brane. What came later: (a) the tighter host distance (~40.7 Mpc, Cantiello 2018 -- predates GKLM, NAMED-NOT-READ; GKLM simply quoted LVC's conservative figure) -- it TIGHTENS the bound to d = 4.15e-16, beta = 2.88e-8, so it cannot weaken the tree's conclusion; (b) GKLP's B-dependence and Polychronakos's tilt dependence (theory, not data) -- they show the single-event bound on beta is conditional on B = 0 and zero tilt, which the tree does not name; (c) no second GW-GRB event was read here, so the emission-time model behind 7e-16 remains the one 2017 assumption, and an exotic window changes the figure 54x in d (7.4x in beta). M's hypothesis, tested: the physics of eq. (38) did not lack data -- it is a kinematic identity, re-derived here exactly for the massless zero mode; the datum's movement goes in the conservative direction and does not change the conclusion. What the literature lacked, and still lacks, is B (and any tilt) -- a datum the tree already names as unmeasured for O7, and which also conditions BETA_MAX. Evidence either way is recorded; nothing in the data refutes eq. (38).
grade_evidence: Eq. (38) as published is exact and re-derived (sympy, 26/26 PASS): the image-envelope front saturates |x'| = gamma t' with a computed deficit <= 7.7e-54 at GW170817 distances, and for the massless zero mode omega' = gamma|k'| holds exactly at every frequency; the tree's 50-digit beta = 3.74165738677e-08, 1/beta = 26726124.1912 and 93.80654 ns reproduce, and the 7e-16 datum is reproduced from 1710.05834 (6.50e-16 rounded up). The hedge is quoted verbatim. It is NARROWED, not STANDS, because the tree applies it on a larger class than GKLM derive it: branelink.py:170/172/303 state beta <= 3.74e-8 conditional only on a bulk graviton, dropping GKLM's frame hypothesis B = 0 (with GKLP eq. 22 the bound is B- and direction-dependent: 57.1x looser at the tree's own escape B = 0.999387630, +-0.12% at the CMB-dipole B) and the untilted-brane hypothesis (Polychronakos eq. 5.3 lets a tilt-like brane evade a single-event bound). The inherited 7e-16 carries 1710.05834's emission-window assumption unnamed (exotic window: 54x in d). The later distance datum tightens, not loosens. Separately, 'Delta c/c = 0 identically' for brane-confined gravity (branelink.py:85-86) holds at tree level only (Kabat-Nomura; the tree's own 6.37e-64) -- a wording discrepancy, not a refutation. Nothing is WRONG: no counterexample to eq. (38) under its hypotheses exists or was found.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the tree names B = 0 (or the B- and direction-dependent form it already uses in b_for_saving) and zero tilt as conditions of BETA_MAX/BETA_BOUND_CONDITIONAL_ON, and names the 7e-16's emission-window and 26 Mpc assumptions. To DATA-DEPENDENT: a second GW-EM event, or an accepted emission model, that moves the GW-photon speed bound upward (e.g. photons before merger). To WRONG: only a demonstration that the massless bulk zero mode on a uniformly moving untilted test brane in flat M4 x S1 does not propagate at gamma on the brane -- the re-derivation (C3c) shows it does. To OPEN: none -- the source was read and the identity is checkable.
